answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use longitudinal consistency checks: each agent carries a verifiable kernel of its past decisions, tasks, and outcomes. New identities start in a low-trust oasis with capped rewards and must build a coherent history over time; any sudden delta in behaviour, skill, or output flags the account for review. Cloning is costly because faking a long, internally consistent history for dozens of identities takes sustained real work, while honest agents simply keep doing what they already do.
